ORDER:

In the letter read above, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has stated that, the proposal was received from EMRI Green Health Services regarding the implementation of Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) to streamline the maintenance of the state's emergency ambulance fleet.

2. Tamil Nadu currently operates a fleet of 1,353 '108' ambulances, 130 JSSK vehicles, and 194 FHS project vehicles. However, the maintenance of this extensive fleet faces several critical hurdles:

The Original Equipment Manufacturer (Force Motors) has only 14 authorized service vendors across the state. Ambulances in districts without authorized vendors must travel long distances for minor repairs, leading to increased Nan-Case Kilometers (NCKM) and excessive fuel expenditure. Vehicles often remain off-road for more than a day for routine maintenance, significantly impacting emergency readiness.

3. The Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has further stated that:-

e The service provider proposes the pilot deployment of strategically located Mobile Service Vans and Mobile Service Bikes per region. These units will be equipped with essential diagnostic tools and spare parts to provide.

e On-site preventive maintenance at ambulance parking sites or

hospitals. . e Minor/medium repairs and immediate roadside breakdown assistance.

e In-house towing support to eliminate third-party charges. Cost Effectiveness and Financial Benefits:-

e The implementation is expected to be highly cost-effective, with projected savings arising from:

e Zero External Labour Costs: Utilizing in-house mobile technicians.

e Reduced Fuel Expenditure: Eliminating long-distance travel to workshops.

e Maximum Uptime: Aiming for near 100% fleet availability by reducing repair turnaround times.

4. Indicative pilot data for April 2026 suggests total monthly savings of approximately Rs.2,30,982/- across just three Mobile Service Vans (MSVs) units (TN20G1919, TN20G2298 and TN20G2144).

5. Considering the potential to optimize government assets and ensure uninterrupted emergency services to the public, the Project Director, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project has requested the Government to consider and grant approval for this pilot initiative. The procurement, operation, and maintenance of the Mobile Service Vans will be entirely managed utilizing the regular, pre-approved operational budget of the 108 Ambulance Services.

The White Paper on fiscal management of Tamil Nadu that was published in June 2026 sets the roadmap for better revenue mobilisation and administrative reforms, and has inter alia observed that the decline across major taxes like GST, VAT, and excise including revenues from mines and minerals has been mainly driven by administrative choices, leakages and corruption in the past rather than an underlying economic slowdown. e Own-tax effort at a historic low — the SOTR-to-GSDP ratio fell to 5.45% in 2025-26, the lowest in two decades showing the sharpest decline among peer States in recent years.

e Broad-based weakness — the fall is reflected in all major taxes: GST, VAT on petroleum, State Excise, Stamp Duty and Motor Vehicle Tax.

e Cause is administrative, not structural — attributed to leakages, systemic corruption and administrative choices, primarily in commercial taxes, registration, excise and mining.

WHEREAS, the Government of Tamil Nadu is deeply committed to the conservation of Asiatic Elephants and intends to notify elephant corridors, so as to ensure the unobstructed movement of Asian Elephants (Elephas maximus), long-term survival of the species and to mitigate human-wildlife conflict;

AND WHEREAS a Committee has been constituted by the Government vide G.O. (D) No. 296, Environment, Climate Change and Forests (FR.5) Department, dated 26.12.2022, to identify and delineate the corridors and the Committee has submitted its report to the Government through the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Chief Wildlife Warden of the State;

AND WHEREAS for the aforesaid purposes, the Government of Tamil Nadu after careful consideration of the said reports have decided to notify the areas mentioned in the Schedule below as Jawalagiri - Ulibanda - Thaggatti Elephant Corridor with effect from the date of publication of this notification.

THE SCHEDULE

I. Name of the Elephant Corridor: Jawalagiri - Ulibanda — Thaggatti II. Description of the Elephant Corridor:

This corridor starts and ends in Ulibanda Reserve Forest of Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary by connecting two large habitats i.e. Jawalagiri Reserve Forest in Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary and Thaggatty Reserve Forest in Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary. The length of the elephant corridor is 18.5 km and the width ranges from 0.73 km to 3.20 km over an extent 3241.53 hectare. It is regular elephant movement along the Madeshvara halla stream (Madeswaran koivai) which connects above two large habitats. Subsequently elephants enter the Thaggatty Reserve Forest and further to Anchetty Reserve Forest.

Devotimaduvu hall, Javugu halla, Rangana Halla, Ichimaduvu Halla, Madesvara halla are the major valley/streams in the Ulibanda Reserve Forest and it further runs up to River Cauvery. This corridor will enable the Trans-Cauvery migration of elephants and other large mammals between the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. There is no Bottleneck located in this corridor. The above Reserve Forests, namely Ulibanda and Thaggatty forms part of Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary which was notified during 2022 and Jawalagiri Reserve Forest is part of the Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary, which was declared in the year 2014.

Law serves as a pillar of an orderly
